subject: Literature
title: Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale
description: One-minute skill: Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale.

hook.text: Atwood made one rule when writing The Handmaid's Tale: nothing in the book could be invented. Everything had happened before.

buildup.text: Gilead is a theocratic state where fertile women are enslaved as 'handmaids' forced to bear children for the elite.

discovery.text: Every atrocity in the novel was drawn from real history: slavery, forced reproduction, religious tyranny, and book burning.

twist.text: The novel's television adaptation made the red handmaid's cloak a real-world protest symbol at political demonstrations.

climax.text: Atwood proved that dystopia is not fantasy but a rearrangement of horrors humanity has already committed.

punchline.text: She did not invent a single atrocity. She only rearranged them.

quiz.question: What was Atwood's key rule when writing The Handmaid's Tale?
options: Every character had to be based on a real person
Nothing in the book could be invented — everything had to have happened before in real history
The story had to be set in a real country
